_about: Hand-maintained rules for /fedramp-lookup/. Each listing is assigned one case by scripts/fedramp/build_lookup.py; each case answers every row. Edit the wording here and push to rebuild. Every case must answer every row, or the build fails. States: lev = package can be leveraged, dec = agency risk decision, no = not recognized, wait = not yet available. {status} in a note is replaced with the listing's marketplace status; {host} with the hosting listing's name. The 'hosted' case is for third-party products a platform lists as services inside its own authorization (see hosted-services.json).

hosted_banner: Listed inside another provider’s authorization. {hostProvider} lists {service} as a service within {host} ({hostId}). The marketplace does not show whether {service} was assessed when it was added. Under CR26, adding a third-party service is a significant change: a third-party assessment of it is recommended, not required, and an assessment report is required only if one was done. Treat {service} as not authorized unless it has its own FedRAMP listing, a FedRAMP Moderate equivalency package, or the {host} package shows significant change testing of its addition. If a vendor gave you {hostId} as this product’s FedRAMP ID, that is the host’s ID, not the product’s.
host_banner: Given this ID for a different product? {hostId} is the ID of {host} itself. The products below are listed as services inside it but have no FedRAMP listing of their own, and the ticks on this card do not extend to them. A vendor quoting this ID for one of them is quoting the host’s authorization, not its own.
pilot_banner: Pilot certification, relabeled {class}. This listing was certified in the FedRAMP 20x pilot on {date}, before certification classes existed; the marketplace later labeled it {class}. FedRAMP’s presumption of adequacy for {class} describes packages built to the CR26 requirements for that class, which this listing was not.
